faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Short answers about using EduBranch AI as a lecturer or a student.
faq.searchPlaceholder: Search questions, e.g. materials, retake, feedback

questions.a: A case-based learning platform for university lecturers and students. Lecturers build cases from course materials; students practise making decisions and read their lecturer's feedback.

questions.q: How do Branching Study and Review Study differ?
questions.a: Branching Study walks through a chain of decision points, each choice leading to a different outcome, and it can be retaken. Review Study is one submission with a solution and its reasoning, which the lecturer reads and answers directly.
There is no automatic grading. AI only asks open questions so students reason more carefully; feedback and assessment belong to the lecturer.

questions.q: Which kinds of materials can I upload?
questions.a: PDF and DOCX files, up to 50 MB each. The system splits them into excerpts and indexes them so AI can cite them.
No. Every case goes through Draft, Reviewed and Approved before Published; students only see a case once the lecturer has approved and published it.

questions.q: Can I write a case without using AI?
questions.a: Yes. Lecturers can create cases with AI or write them from scratch; both go through the same review process before opening to the class.
In Branching Study you can retake a case to try another course of action and review each attempt. A Review Study submission is final and cannot be edited.

questions.q: When will I see my lecturer's feedback?
questions.a: As soon as the lecturer has read your work and sent feedback; it appears on the result page of the attempt or submission.

questions.q: Does AI use materials from other courses?
questions.a: No. AI drafts and asks questions based on the materials the lecturer uploaded for that course.

questions.q: Who chooses the AI model the system uses?
questions.a: The AI model is configured by the university on the server; administrators monitor the AI service. Lecturers and students do not need to choose.
